notes: Qualified enterprise opportunity. Amberfield is a payment processing and risk platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production inference of chat-based merchant support assistants and a real-time reranking service used by fraud workflows. Primary asks: firm throughput guarantees for peak batch windows (peak 5k rps aggregated; sustained 2.5k rps), strict latency SLOs (p99 <= 120ms for chat token generation, p50 < 20ms), deterministic cold-start behavior, and predictable reserved GPU planning (pilot: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs; target steady-state: 32 GPUs). Autoscaling discussion items: scale-up policy (CPU/GPU util thresholds, request queue depth), scale-down cool-down to avoid flapping, warm-pool of pre-warmed worker containers to shave cold-start; desired warm-pool size estimate 2–4 instances per availability zone. Queueing behavior: they want bounded queue depth, backpressure strategy (429 vs. queuing with ETA), and metrics exposed for live throttling. Cost sensitivity high — asked for unit cost estimates across batching and quantization profiles; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations. Security/compliance: company requires SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key control, audit logs retention 7 years, and EU data residency for EU customers. Direct quote from Head of Infrastructure, Alex Mercer: "We need hard p99 guarantees; bursts cannot impact transaction flows."
